state.summary: A product team suspects onboarding friction but does not yet know the main cause.
known_facts: the current evidence does not isolate one cause
constraints: the full user base must not be exposed to an unproven change
feedback should arrive before any broader rollout

tension.summary: The team needs new evidence without turning a weak hypothesis into a system-wide decision.

cause.summary: A confusing first step may be contributing to onboarding abandonment.
supporting_signals: drop-off occurs near the first setup step
two support messages mention unclear wording
cause.basis: Early behavioral signals and limited user feedback

transition.to: observed evidence from a bounded pilot
transition.trigger: need to distinguish the suspected cause from alternatives
transition.expected_consequence: The team gains evidence without changing onboarding for the full user base.

participants.name: product owner
participants.risk: treating a weak signal as proof

participants.name: support team
participants.risk: drawing conclusions from too few cases

cooperation.shared_upside: The suspected cause can be tested while exposure and recovery cost remain limited.

action.summary: Run the revised first step with five consenting pilot users and keep the original flow available.
action.review_after: after five pilot sessions or the first harmful signal
